squash_audit.reasoning: Claude Opus 4.6 marker commit commit AI AI_ROOT_CAUSE / AI_DIRECT_ROOT CONFIRM

code_evidence.summary: Claude-assisted Synology Chat code replaced the webhook's stable numeric recipient with a lookup by mutable nickname or username, so a colliding account could receive another user's reply.
code_evidence.mechanism: The webhook handler resolved payload.username through the Chat user list and passed that result to the outbound send path instead of retaining payload.user_id.

steps.title: AI change
steps.detail: The Claude-coauthored squash added nickname and username resolution and used the result as the recipient for immediate and buffered replies.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The direct fix keeps replies on the webhook's stable user_id by default and permits name matching only behind an explicitly dangerous compatibility flag.

candidate_hunks.annotation: The Claude-coauthored change resolves a stable webhook user ID through mutable nickname or username data, then carries that resolved value into direct reply delivery. A renamed or colliding account can therefore redirect the bot's response.
The channel uses the resolved chatUserId as the recipient for buffered replies. This completes the vulnerable path from mutable name matching to the outbound send target.

fix_hunks.annotation: Account resolution now defaults the compatibility flag to false. Deployments that do nothing therefore retain the stable numeric webhook recipient instead of entering mutable-name lookup.
The reply resolver now returns the stable payload user_id before any nickname or username lookup unless an operator deliberately enables the dangerous compatibility mode.

squash_audit.reasoning: webhook commit Claude Opus 4.6 co-author commit PR TP => CONFIRM

code_evidence.summary: Claude-coauthored webhook code treated caller-supplied sender and chat_id fields as authenticated identity while request authentication was optional, allowing a remote caller to impersonate an allowlisted sender and steer message routing.
code_evidence.mechanism: The handler checked its allowlist against payload.sender and built the inbound session from payload.sender and payload.chat_id; the default auth_token was None, so reachable deployments could accept those claims without proof.

steps.title: AI change
steps.detail: The Claude-coauthored commit created the webhook with optional authentication and made both authorization and routing depend on identity fields supplied in JSON.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The direct fix defaults to server-configured sender and chat identifiers, fails startup without a fixed sender, and makes payload identity an explicit legacy opt-in.

+pub struct WebhookChannelConfig {
+    /// Address to bind the HTTP server to.
+    pub bind_address: String,
+    /// Port to listen on.
+    pub port: u16,
+    /// URL path to accept webhook requests on.
+    pub path: String,
+    /// Optional Bearer token for request authentication.
+    /// When set, all requests must include a matching `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
+    pub auth_token: Option<String>,
+}
+
+impl Default for WebhookChannelConfig {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            bind_address: "127.0.0.1".to_string(),
+            port: 9876,
+            path: "/webhook".to_string(),
+            auth_token: None,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// JSON body expected from webhook POST requests.
+#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
+struct WebhookPayload {
+    /// The message content.
+    message: String,
+    /// Identifier of the sender.
+    sender: String,
+    /// Chat/conversation identifier for session routing.
+    chat_id: String,
+}
candidate_hunks.annotation: The new webhook defaults Bearer authentication to None and defines sender and chat_id as mandatory client-controlled JSON fields. Nothing in this configuration binds those claims to the caller.

The new resolver fails closed when no fixed sender is configured and returns server-owned sender and chat values by default. Caller-supplied fields are used only inside the explicit trust_payload_identity compatibility branch.
Authorization and inbound routing now consume only the resolved identity. The request body no longer directly supplies the allowlist principal or the session chat identifier.
Startup stops when the secure mode lacks a configured sender_id. This prevents an operator mistake from silently falling back to caller-controlled identity.
